p: So this is it. Your new home. It's… very long.
Fifty-seven feet of pure luxury. Come in — mind your head.
Ow. Too late. Honestly, Maya, I thought you'd be back in a flat by now. It must be freezing in winter.

p.r: a lot warmer than you'd think

p: . This little stove heats the whole boat in ten minutes.
OK, but you must be lonely out here. It's just you and the ducks.
Lonely? With this lot? They start quacking at six every morning.
And Admiral? Cats hate water. He must be miserable.

p.r: a lot happier than you'd think

p: . He's basically the captain now. He sits on the roof and yells at the swans.

gloss.m: a long, narrow boat people live on
be careful, the door is low
a small heater you burn wood in
control which way a boat goes
the flat outside part of a boat

p: a lot / much + -er: warmer, harder, nicer
more + long adjective: more spacious · fun → more fun
gloss.m: funnier comes from funny (= makes you laugh)

steps.note: Also possible: a lot cosier than you'd think (for warmer) · much / way happier (for happier). Just happier, not <s>more happier</s>.

p: Right. And driving it must be easy. It's one long, straight canal.

p.r: a lot harder than you'd think

p: . I've hit the same bridge three times.
Of course it did. And will you stop saying "than you'd think"?

p.r: a lot harder than you'd think
a lot nicer than I thought

p: Told you. So, are you staying for dinner?
Dinner? Where would we even sit?
Will the ducks be joining us?
They always do. And Admiral eats first. He's the captain.

steps.note: Also possible: a lot trickier / more difficult than you'd think (for the first harder) · a lot better than I thought (for Dan's nicer). About your own expectation: than I thought (Dan's line); what people in general expect: than you'd think. Just harder, not <s>more harder</s> or <s>less harder</s>.
